evidence: ATTRIBUTION_GAP: Searched decls.jsonl for the predicate by name and by kind (see `searched`); the content appears only as NavierStokes.SlowBorelBase.baseVelocity_smooth (SlowBorelBase.lean:1194), NavierStokes.BaseResidual.basePressure_smooth (BaseResidual.lean:1496) and NavierStokes.ParametricRadialExtension.descent_contDiffOn (ParametricRadialExtension.lean:134).

CONVENTION: NavierStokes.ParametricEvenDescent.contDiffOn_descend (ParametricEvenDescent.lean:213) and its X = R²/2 rescaling NavierStokes.ParametricRadialExtension.descent_contDiffOn (ParametricRadialExtension.lean:134) take `ContDiff ℝ ∞ F` plus `EvenRadial F` as hypotheses.

Definition 3.2 is terminology, and the Lean repository never names it: repeated searches of the 52,516-declaration index by name, by kind and by docstring vocabulary found no predicate. Both of its clauses are nevertheless stated, for general objects, and in the paper's own ranges — Cartesian C^∞ on Iio 1 ×ˢ univ for the background velocity and pressure, and C^∞ on Ici 0 ×ˢ univ in (X, η) for even radial profiles with the X = R²/2 normalisation written into the docstring. The gap is packaging, and the recovery is a one-line conjunction plus the standard even-descent equivalence, so the relation is different_formulation and the verdict OK.

findings.summary: No Lean declaration defines the predicate 'regular at the axis'. Both clauses are stated, but inlined as ContDiffOn assertions in four separate modules rather than packaged as one definition that later statements quantify over.

Clause (ii) is encoded in the opposite direction: Lean assumes a C^∞ germ even in the signed radius and concludes smoothness in X up to X = 0, where the paper simply posits a smooth extension in (X,eta) to X = 0.
